 Trump made 700+ stock trades in September, including AI companies. Erin Burnett reports. 
 2:47
 President Donald Trump made more than 700 stock transactions in September, including buying and selling thousands of dollars in tech company shares in the weeks leading up the White House’s high-profile artificial intelligence summit .
 The trades marked the continuation of Trump’s unprecedented pace of investment activity while in office, which has drawn scrutiny from critics over the president’s ability to personally profit off his presidency.
 In a statement, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle denied that Trump has any control over his investment accounts, saying the portfolio is independently managed by “third-party financial institutions.”
 The most recent trades, which were disclosed in a new filing with the Office of Government Ethics, included the purchase and sale of stock in companies whose CEOs later attended Trump’s closely watched AI summit. During that meeting, Trump endorsed a hands-off approach to regulating the AI industry based on assurances the companies would “self-police” their activities.
 Those trades included early-September purchases of hundreds of thousands of dollars of stock in Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon — as well as purchases of tens of thousands of dollars of stock in Palantir and Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
 Trump separately also sold some stock in Nvidia, Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. The filing did not disclose any trading activity in the four days directly leading up to the September 29 AI summit.

 White House national cyber director set to be replaced
 According to sources speaking to CNN, White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is set to leave his position and be replaced by Kirsten Davies, the Senate-confirmed chief information officer at the Defense Department.
 0:45
 • Source:
 CNN 
 White House national cyber director set to be replaced 
 0:45
 Sean Cairncross is being replaced as the White House national cyber director, administration officials confirmed on social media Thursday — a move which comes as the nation is still reeling from a string of cyber outages .
 The exact circumstances of Cairncross’ departure were not immediately clear, but a source to the White House said President Donald Trump “fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position as he lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job.”
 The White House had previously touted Cairncross’s “extensive leadership experience” when he was confirmed to the role in 2025.
 Cairncross was nominated by Trump and served as the Senate-confirmed national cyber director for more than a year. He also played a key role in the administration’s dealings with major AI firms.
 Kirsten Davies, the Senate-confirmed chief information officer at the Defense Department, will take over the role in an acting capacity, the source said. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Davies in social media posts Thursday, with Hegseth writing she has “proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional.”

 Trump returns from his trilateral summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin
 2:35
 • Source:
 CNN 
 Trump returns from his trilateral summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin 
 2:35
 Officials were frank heading into Thursday’s unprecedented three-way talks: US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin were unlikely to leave Shenzhen with any major agreements.
 Diplomatic breakthroughs, it turned out, were not the point. The talks themselves were the deliverable. Eighty-one minutes was hardly enough time to resolve all the major differences between the three countries, on wars, economics and cutting-edge technology.
 Here are five takeaways from the summit : 
 Competing objectives: Putin initially proposed the summit to discuss Ukraine without Kyiv present, alarming Ukrainian officials and drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference. Both Xi and Putin invoked that era in their opening remarks, hinting at how they viewed Thursday’s meeting. US officials initially said Ukraine would not be on the agenda, though Trump later said he would raise it. The US president’s priority was a nuclear arms control pact with Moscow and Beijing, though he acknowledged the obstacles.
 Building diplomatic bonds: The relationships on display are complicated. Trump has worked ardently to cultivate both Xi and Putin over the last two years, hoping deeper personal ties will translate into smoother geopolitics. “We are really making history,” Trump said proudly. “The three of us have a great deal to discuss.” He’s employed flattery and showy summits to fete and elevate his counterparts, but the flattery has yet to yield significant breakthroughs.
 Wars shaping the summit: Trump’s war in Iran and Putin’s war in Ukraine have each sapped military resources and led to global price increases — and frustrated Xi, who sees the conflicts as a threat to global stability. Both wars were topics Trump hoped to discuss with Xi and Putin, each of whom maintains ties with Tehran.
 AI race: Trump arrived in China amid a scandal involving Nvidia’s CEO and cascading service outages in the United States , caused in some cases by AI updates. Against the backdrop of this gleaming hub of China’s tech and chipmaking industries, questions about how the US will compete in the rapidly developing AI industry seemed more urgent.
 Xi as a diplomatic power player: Beijing will see this summit as a major success for Chinese diplomacy. Trump’s praise of China and his assurances that as long as he and Xi are in charge they’ll “never have a problem” are welcome words for a Chinese leadership that’s closely watching for a tone shift in US policy toward China amid growing calls from US lawmakers to tighten controls on Chinese access to US high-tech.

 Trump will hold a news conference at the White House today
 By Molly English and Donald Judd 
 President Donald Trump announced today’s White House news conference on his return flight from a diplomatic blitz in Asia.
 The president is expected to speak at noon ET.
 It follows this week’s historic trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
 “Heading back to Washington, D.C., from China. It was a Great and Highly Consequential Trip,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday aboard Air Force One.
 “I will be giving a News Conference tomorrow at 12 P.M., the White House. Also, will be discussing the Trade Deals with Thailand, the Philippines, and others.”
 When he returned to the White House on Thursday evening after the 15-hour flight, he declined to answer questions about whether he’d meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
